claim_summary: TimeRLM makes long time-series queryable through iterative code execution, while the work contributes RL post-training and AnomalyXL to evaluate precise anomaly localization.

claim_evidence.quote: We therefore introduce TimeRLM, an RLM formulation that enables manipulating time-series signals as external context, querying them over multiple turns in a sandboxed Python environment, and reasoning through code and vision to submit a structured answer grounded in the underlying signal.
introduce AnomalyXL, an open-source benchmark measuring precise anomaly localization in long horizon timeseries spanning two evaluation corpora, AnomalyXL-MCQ and AnomalyXL-Localize.
We posttrain TimeRLM with a Qwen3.5-4B RLM backbone using

modules.name: Temporal code interaction runtime
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK is no: the runtime does not encode an anomaly output or verifier, and its code actions need not be redesigned for another task family. R3_2_GTS is yes: it exposes and operates on an ordered time-series as external state.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:no - no task-family output or verifier is embedded
R3_2_GTS:yes - the external state is an ordered time-series queried and manipulated over time
R4:Interface and Interaction; Memory and Context; Tools and Execution; Planning and Orchestration

evidence.quote: A JSON object containing the time-series is pre-defined as a variable. This setup allows the model to operate over the full recording directly through code (Fig. 1).
code returns an observation ot = exec(ct , st ) for t ≥ 1 appended to the history, and the episode terminates with a single verifiable reward r(ŷ, y) ∈ [0, 1].

modules.name: AnomalyXL benchmark and scoring
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK is yes: AnomalyXL defines anomaly-localization outputs and task-specific scorers; changing task family requires replacing its task schemas and validation criteria. The resource tests other systems rather than serving as their general runtime.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - anomaly-localization output schemas and scoring criteria are task-specific

evidence.quote: AnomalyXL is a long-context, multi-channel benchmark for evidence-grounded anomaly localization: every answer requires precise retrieval of a time span, channel, or magnitude
Each precise row is scored by a deterministic function of the model’s final message that returns a value in [0, 1]. The same value is used as the evaluation score and, during RL, as the reward.

modules.name: GRPO-trained anomaly workflow policy
modules.scope_reason: This module updates the LLM policy with GRPO rewards from anomaly-localization workflow rollouts, so it changes model action selection from workflow feedback.

evidence.quote: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) (Shao et al. 2024) on AnomalyXL-Localize, with full-parameter tuning and no supervised warm start.
Rather than relying on a fixed training set, we integrate the generator directly into the training loop: every step synthesizes a fresh batch of recordings, so no sample repeats within a run.

task_performance.quote: TimeRLM (image, GPT-5.5) leads on localization with 0.682 IoU, against 0.329 for the best single-pass variant and 0.323 for fine-tuned 32B Toto. On classify-with-evidence every baseline stays below 0.05 while TimeRLM reaches 0.745.

changes: dimensions: Coordination and Scaling -> Planning and Orchestration; add Interface and Interaction; retain Memory and Context and Tools and Execution
reconciliation.reason: The existing runtime mechanism is the same, but its state is a queryable time-series exposed for code operations, meeting R3_2_GTS. It also supports temporal data management and processing.

changes: dimensions: Control, Verification, and Feedback -> Planning and Orchestration
reconciliation.reason: AnomalyXL is a task-specific benchmark resource. Its anomaly outputs and deterministic temporal scoring meet R3_1_TSK, while its role is to evaluate other systems.
The contribution is a GRPO-trained LLM policy that selects actions in an anomaly-localization workflow from verifiable rollout rewards; LLM modules use llm_route and no Harness dimensions.

items.reason: The recording X in R^{C x L} is exposed as a queryable variable over which code windows and slices channels and time spans; its state and action semantics depend on ordered multichannel series and is not bound to one task family (same sandbox for localize/classify/magnitude).

adjudication.summary: Candidate accepted unchanged. The sandbox is task-independent but depends on temporal addressing of the recording, so GTS rather than GH.
